scope: Conversation tests, automatic operation failure screenshots, benchmark comparisons and redacted support bundles. Scheduling and notification features are deferred.

failure_screenshots.capture: First observed browser failure before cleanup and browser queue release; never navigates or signs in to get an image
failure_screenshots.privacy: Form controls and unrelated frames are masked; authentication pages are refused. Other visible FBS text may contain private booking data, so images are separate from redacted support bundles.
failure_screenshots.limits: One image up to 4 MiB per failed/unknown operation, bounded by the existing operation count/TTL. No image is promised when no browser exists, the page changes, capture fails or authentication is present. No images survive restart. Screenshot failures do not alter write outcomes or trigger retries.

support_bundle.included: Operation ID/kind/status/times, setup-check names/statuses, at most 100 task-local events with timings, exception type and code locations
support_bundle.excluded: Raw log files, raw exception messages, URLs, configuration values/paths, credentials, cookies, MFA prompts, booking references/details/purpose, contacts, screenshots and amendment comparison keys
support_bundle.retention: Traces follow existing in-memory operation retention. Recovered write history has no historical trace or image.
support_bundle.interpretation: The bundle is diagnostic evidence, not proof of success, empty availability or safe retry. Reconcile uncertain writes.

backend_regression_comparison.inputs: Completed benchmark reports with identical comparison_context and unique case names
backend_regression_comparison.defaults: At least five samples; flag success-latency growth exceeding both 20 percent and 100 ms, or failure-rate growth of at least five percentage points

exit_codes.2: Invalid inputs, unmatched/skipped cases or insufficient samples

backend_regression_comparison.limits: Threshold alerts are not statistical significance tests. Successful latency does not hide failed samples. Backend timings and structured response bytes are not model token or end-to-end speed savings.

conversation_evaluation.selection: Repeat --case CASE_ID to run selected cases from benchmarks/conversation_cases.json
conversation_evaluation.isolation: Actual noninteractive Codex calls use only a synthetic Sagasu MCP. Both MCP packages come from immutable Git snapshots; the baseline defaults to 51fb3a2. No real .env, FBS session/profile, saved contacts or live booking writes are used. Unimplemented fixture operations fail instead of falling through to FBS.
conversation_evaluation.measurement: Full CLI-reported input/output/cached/reasoning tokens, end-to-end elapsed time including CLI startup and tool exchanges, MCP/command counts, tool names, independently graded room/time coverage and native fixture write counts
conversation_evaluation.conversations: Clarification cases include an initial request and a follow-up. Follow-ups replay the user/assistant text into a fresh CLI task and fixture context; they do not test Codex resume or shared-host continuation.
conversation_evaluation.ordering: Baseline/candidate order alternates across repetitions. Real model calls require explicit --run and are excluded from ordinary unit tests/CI.
conversation_evaluation.interpretation: Only compare savings when both arms pass the same correctness checks. Fewer calls alone are insufficient. Under three repetitions is exploratory; retain raw sample variation and review results rather than asserting significance or universal savings. Real FBS latency and user-specific Codex configuration are outside this synthetic comparison.
conversation_evaluation.coverage: Reports enumerate unevaluated feature IDs. Features not exercised by the dataset remain subject to the agreed evaluation policy; this harness does not establish their retention case automatically.
